samples.text:
In recent years, some governments have made laws to stop people using single-use plastic items like bags, straws and cups. In my opinion, this is a positive development, even though it can be inconvenient for some people at first.

The most important reason is that plastic is very harmful for the environment. Single-use items are used only for few minutes, but they stay in nature for hundreds of years. A lot of this plastic go into rivers and the sea, where fish and birds eat it and die. On many beaches, people can see bottles and bags everywhere, which is also bad for tourism. If these products are banned, the amount of rubbish will reduce a lot.

Another reason is that the ban changes people's habits. When shops stop giving free plastic bags, customers start to bring their own cloth bags. In my country, for example, after the government ban plastic bags, most people quickly got used to carry reusable bags, and now it is normal. So a law can teach people to think more about the environment in their daily life.

However, some people argue that the ban is not fair for small businesses, because paper or metal products is more expensive. Also, some disabled people need plastic straws to drink. These are real problems, but the government can help businesses with the cost and allow special exceptions.

In conclusion, I strongly believe that banning single-use plastic is a positive step, because it protects the environment and helps people to develop better habits. The small problems it cause are much less important than the benefits for nature.
samples.why: Clear positive position · relevant ideas with a personal example but limited depth · basic linking · adequate topic vocabulary · several errors in agreement, verb forms and articles.

samples.text:
A number of countries have recently passed laws prohibiting single-use plastic items such as carrier bags, straws and disposable cups. Although these bans create some short-term difficulties, I firmly believe they are a positive development.

The main argument in favour is the scale of the environmental damage caused by disposable plastic. These products are typically used for a few minutes but can take centuries to break down, and a large proportion of them ends up in rivers and oceans rather than being recycled. Marine animals frequently become trapped in plastic waste or mistake it for food, and tiny plastic particles are now found in the food chain. Banning the most common items therefore tackles the problem at its source rather than relying on clean-up campaigns.

In addition, legislation is often more effective than voluntary change. For years, people have been encouraged to reuse bags and avoid plastic straws, yet many continued to use them simply out of habit. When a ban is introduced, alternatives quickly become the norm; customers remember to bring their own bags, and cafes switch to paper or reusable options. Such laws also send a clear message that protecting the environment is a shared responsibility.

Critics point out that substitutes can be more expensive and that some people, including certain disabled individuals, genuinely rely on plastic straws. These are valid concerns, but they can be addressed through sensible exemptions and temporary support for small businesses, rather than by abandoning the policy altogether.

In conclusion, while bans on single-use plastic cause some inconvenience, the long-term benefits for wildlife, oceans and human health are far greater. For this reason, I consider them a clearly positive development.
samples.why: Clear position throughout · well-extended ideas on environmental damage and behaviour change · counter-argument answered · good cohesion · appropriate less common vocabulary · mostly error-free, one agreement slip.

samples.text:
Governments in several countries have moved beyond encouraging responsible consumption and have begun to outlaw disposable plastic products altogether. Although such bans are sometimes dismissed as symbolic or inconvenient, I regard them as an unequivocally positive development.

The environmental rationale is difficult to dispute. Items such as straws and carrier bags serve their purpose for minutes yet persist in the environment for generations, and because they are light and cheap, they are among the items most likely to escape waste systems and end up in waterways. Once there, they entangle wildlife, break down into microplastics and ultimately return to humans through the food chain. Restricting their production addresses the problem at its origin, which is far more efficient than attempting to retrieve plastic once it has dispersed across coastlines and seabeds.

Equally significant is the effect such laws have on behaviour. Decades of public awareness campaigns achieved only modest results, largely because individual consumers had little incentive to abandon a convenient habit. A ban, by contrast, removes the choice and in doing so rapidly establishes a new social norm: carrying a reusable bag or cup soon feels unremarkable rather than virtuous. This shift can also stimulate innovation, as manufacturers compete to develop durable or biodegradable alternatives.

Opponents raise two legitimate objections. Replacement materials can be costlier for small retailers, and some people with disabilities depend on flexible plastic straws. Neither point, however, undermines the principle of a ban. Both can be accommodated through carefully designed exemptions and transitional support, and some substitutes carry their own environmental costs, which argues for promoting reuse rather than for retaining plastic.

In conclusion, laws against single-use plastics tackle a serious environmental threat directly and reshape everyday habits in a way that persuasion alone has failed to do. Provided they are implemented with appropriate flexibility, they deserve wholehearted support.
samples.why: Unequivocal, well-argued judgement · ideas extended with clear causal reasoning · objections evaluated convincingly · skilful paragraphing and cohesion · precise, wide-ranging vocabulary · complex structures used accurately.
